name: Replicate
look: Warm cream canvas with 128px display type, hot orange reserved for the CTA and hero band, and dark code wells as pull-quotes.

hero.title: Run open-source models with one line of code
hero.sub: Thousands of community models, packaged and versioned, callable from any language. You pay by the second and only while a model is actually running.

features.title: Someone else already packaged it
features.sub: Every model arrives containerised, versioned and with a typed input schema, so running it is an API call rather than a weekend.

items.title: Packaged models
items.body: Each model is a container with a declared schema. No dependency hell, no CUDA archaeology.

items.title: Per-second billing
items.body: You pay while the model runs and nothing while it does not. Cold starts are not billed.

items.title: Versioned
items.body: Every model has an immutable version hash, so a result you got last year is reproducible today.

items.title: Push your own
items.body: Wrap any model with a small config file and deploy it with one command.

items.title: Scales to zero
items.body: Traffic spikes scale out automatically and back to nothing. No cluster to keep warm.

items.title: Webhooks
items.body: Long-running predictions call you back rather than holding a connection open.

showcases.title: A version hash, not a moving target
showcases.body: Models are pinned to an immutable version. When a maintainer ships an update it becomes a new version rather than silently changing the behaviour of the one you already shipped against.
points: Full input and output logged per prediction

showcases.title: Push your own model in an afternoon
showcases.body: Write a small config declaring your inputs and a predict function. One command builds the container, pushes it, and gives you an API endpoint with a generated schema and playground.
points: One config file and one command

gallery.title: Explore
gallery.sub: A slice of what the community has published this month.

testimonial.quote: We shipped an image feature in two days because somebody had already packaged the model properly. The alternative was three weeks and a GPU cluster nobody wanted to own.
testimonial.name: Rosa Delgado

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Pay by the second of compute. Nothing while idle.

items.a: You are billed for the seconds a prediction actually runs on hardware. Cold-start time is not billed, and an idle model costs nothing.

items.q: Can I run a private model?
items.a: Yes. Push it with the same tooling as a public one and it stays visible only to your account, with the same API shape.

items.q: What happens when a model updates?
items.a: Nothing to your integration. Updates become new immutable versions; the version you pinned keeps working indefinitely.
The maintainer declares the requirement and we schedule accordingly, from a T4 up to an H100. The tier used is shown on every prediction.

cta.title: Run your first model
cta.sub: Sign in with GitHub and get $10 of credit. No card.

footer.tagline: Run open-source models with an API.

notes: Warm cream replaces white as the canvas, with a bone tint for inset cards.
Hot orange is reserved for the primary CTA, the hero band and inline links. It is never decorative.
Display headlines run enormous — up to 128px in hero bands — at line-height 1.0 with negative tracking.
Every interactive element is fully rounded; content cards step back to a modest 10px.
Dark code wells sit inside the cream canvas as full-bleed reading surfaces, functioning like print pull-quotes.
